assessable_statement_group: Standard symbols show electrical connections, not the physical shapes or positions of equipment. Learn the cell, battery, open/closed switch, lamp, fixed resistor, variable resistor, ammeter, voltmeter, diode, LED, thermistor and LDR, plus the fuse (a rectangle with a continuous line through it). A cell uses one long/short line pair; a battery uses multiple pairs. Junctions and continuous wires define connections.

assessable_statement_group: Electric current is the rate of flow of electric charge. A source of potential difference is needed to sustain current in a closed conducting circuit. In a metal the mobile charges are electrons; conventional current is drawn in the opposite direction, from positive to negative through the external circuit. Our moving dots show conventional direction, not electron drift speed.

assessable_statement_group: Charge flow Q, current I and time t obey Q=It. Use coulombs C, amperes A and seconds s. A current of 1 A means 1 C passes a cross-section each second. For 0.5 A over 8 s, Q=4 C. The animation counts cumulative charge past a reference line; it does not count charge being created inside the cell.

assessable_statement_group: The current is the same at every point in a single closed loop. assessable_statement_group: Current through a component depends on the potential difference across it and its resistance. Use V=IR, with volts V, amperes A and ohms Ω. Rearrange to I=V/R or R=V/I. Potential difference describes the electrical drive across two points; current describes through-flow. Their units and measuring connections differ.
